newsitem.title: UK: UK house prices to rise 7.0 percent in 1996 - UBS.
newsitem.headline: UK house prices to rise 7.0 percent in 1996 - UBS.

text.p: UK house prices will rise by seven percent this year and 10 percent in 1997, according to analysts at UBS.
The UBS forecasts for the housing market have been revised upwards. Up to now, the Swiss bank was predicting five percent house price inflation this year, rising to six in 1997.

"These revisions reflect the increasingly vigorous nature of the recovery in the housing market," said Rob Thomas, building societies analyst at UBS. Thomas said price gains will be most pronounced in London and the South East. There, prices will rise 12 percent this year and 15 percent next, he forecast.

Transactions -- the number of houses bought and sold -- will be only four percent up on 1995 this year. "There is now a serious shortage of both new and second hand properties coming onto the market in many areas," Thomas said.
He said UBS was among the most bullish forecasters for house prices but one of the most bearish on transactions.

There will be better news on negative equity, where property owners find the value of their property is less than the mortgage taken out on it. Thomas forecast the number of households with negative equity will fall to 500,000 by the final quarter of this year and just 90,000 by the end of 1997.
